plan.title: Commit-shape check (#5656) refuses Bash calls whose heredoc text merely mentions a commit command

narratives.Description: The #5656 commit-shape check reads the whole Bash command text, so a heredoc body that only names a commit command (for example a note appended to a file) is treated as a commit and can be refused with the -a/pathspecs message. This story exports the authz preprocess chain (line continuations removed, then heredoc bodies removed) from `packages/core/src/authz/classify.ts` and runs it inside every commit-shape detector in `packages/core/src/hooks/commit-target.ts` before tokenizing. Real commits, compound `cd <abs> && git commit -F <file>` forms and -a/pathspec refusals stay as they are; non-heredoc string literals stay residual.
narratives.UserStory: As a worker agent writing notes through Bash, I want heredoc text that only names a commit command to be ignored by the commit-shape check, so that I can record the real cause without rewording it.
narratives.ImplementationPlan: One product PR (deft-story: 6187). 1. `packages/core/src/authz/classify.ts`: add one exported helper that returns `zipShellWithoutHereDocBodies(zipShellWithoutLineContinuations(command))`, and use it at the two existing authz call sites. 2. `packages/core/src/hooks/commit-target.ts`: one private function tokenizes the sanitized command; `commandHasGitCommitSubcommand`, `commandHasGitCommitIndexMutatingForm` and `resolveCommitTarget` (the checkout-retarget detector since #6278) all use it, so the prospective-cover entry in dispatcher.ts, which calls them, sees the same sanitized text. 3. Fixtures in `packages/core/src/hooks/commit-target.test.ts` and an end-to-end hook test in the new `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher-commit-heredoc.test.ts`. 4. Changelog fragment `changelog.d/6187-commit-shape-heredoc-bodies.md`. The detectors moved from dispatcher.ts to commit-target.ts after the lean was written (#6278), so the lean's dispatcher.ts / dispatcher.test.ts rows map to commit-target.ts and a new dispatcher test file; dispatcher.ts itself needs no edit.
narratives.Overview:
- relieves: P1, P2, P3 — Shared sanitize: export/share the authz preprocess chain `zipShellWithoutHereDocBodies(zipShellWithoutLineContinuations(…))` (quoted and unquoted delimiters; preserve commands before/after; unclosed early-return residual); do not fork a third lexer.
- relieves: P1, P2, P3 — Detector-wide apply: every exported #5656 detector (`commandHasGitCommitSubcommand`, index-mutating, checkout-retarget) and the prospective-cover entry must run that shared sanitize before split/token scan so production entry and unit-test helper calls cannot diverge.
- relieves: P1, P2, P3 — Proof fixtures: quoted-heredoc note that mentions a commit (issue repro, including `&&` inside the body) must not match subcommand/index-mutating; real `cd <wt> && git … -F <file>` still matches subcommand and stays non-mutating; real `-am` / trailing pathspecs still refuse; line-continued heredoc opener covered via shared chain; unclosed heredoc residual stays residual.
- CHANGELOG Unreleased notes the false-positive fix; Refs #6187 / #5656.

## In plain English

The #5656 commit-shape gate must classify only commands the shell will run. Text inside a recognized heredoc body is data, so a note that merely names a commit command must not fire the commit check. Strip heredoc bodies before the existing detectors; keep real compound commits and -a/pathspec refuses.

## Bound remedy

- Strip recognized heredoc bodies (quoted and unquoted delimiters; preserve commands before/after) before `commandHasGitCommitSubcommand` / index-mutating / checkout-retarget / prospective cover — reuse or share the authz `zipShellWithoutHereDocBodies` pattern (export/shared helper; do not fork a third lexer).
- Apply the strip once at the commit-shape entry so every #5656 detector sees the same sanitized command.
- Proof fixtures: quoted-heredoc note that mentions a commit (issue repro, including `&&` inside the body) must not match subcommand/index-mutating; real `cd <wt> && git … -F <file>` still matches subcommand and stays non-mutating; real `-am` / trailing pathspecs still refuse; unclosed heredoc residual stays residual.
- CHANGELOG Unreleased notes the false-positive fix; Refs #6187 / #5656.

## Reject

- Disable the commit-shape gate
- Docs-only “reword the note” guidance as the product fix
- Strip only quoted heredocs and leave unquoted bodies matched
- Full shell AST / new parser as co-equal ship for this ticket
- Absorb #6185 launch-root / multi-eligible write binding into this Bound
- Treat obscured non-heredoc forms as in-scope (remain hooks-installed / `--no-verify` residual)

## Footnotes (non-mechanism)

- Live tip repro on dispatch-sha: quoted heredoc mentioning a commit returns hasCommit true (false positive). Trailing prose after a fake `-F` token can flip index-mutating and emit the -a/pathspecs deny message seen in the issue.
- Issue Related line cites #6185 for compound-commit refuse; open #6185 is a different launch-root bug. Prefer-A keeps compound detection; do not retarget that issue here.
- Authz already strips heredoc bodies for zip/protected-dest classification; Prefer-A is share-or-export that strip into the hooks commit-shape path.

Open critique of Prefer-A draft 6807906781 (conflict_group commit-shape-heredoc-body-false-positive). Ceiling 6807907162. Pin-read `git show e514bc81132ff8c3bfbb5f9cdf6490d80bfcdc5a:` for hooks commit-shape + authz heredoc strip. No product implement.

## Inventory (existing mechanisms)

- `commandHasGitCommitSubcommand` / `commandHasGitCommitIndexMutatingForm` / `commandHasGitCommitCheckoutRetarget` / `decideProspectiveGitCommitScopeCover` in `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts` (#5656). Detectors split the raw command on `&&` / `||` / `;` / newlines, then token-scan each part. Obscured forms stay hooks-installed / `--no-verify` residual by comment.
- Authz already sanitizes shell text for zip/protected-dest via private `zipShellWithoutLineContinuations` then `zipShellWithoutHereDocBodies` in `packages/core/src/authz/classify.ts` (quoted and unquoted delimiters; preserves commands before/after; unclosed heredoc returns early). Hooks already import `../authz` — share/export that strip; do not fork a third lexer.
- Existing #5656 fixtures cover compound status-then-commit, index-mutating refuse, and quoted message allow; no heredoc-body false-positive fixture yet.

## Re-verify

Issue repro with a body that names a compound commit-with-file form splits into a fake commit part before any heredoc strip. That matches Prefer-A / Stop 1 P1–P3: hasCommit true on non-executed text; trailing tokens after a fake file-message flag can trip index-mutating and emit the pathspecs deny. Prefer-A strip-first at commit-shape entry is the correct order relative to those detectors. Reject list is right: keep real compound detection (#6185 stays separate); do not disable the gate; do not docs-only; do not quoted-only strip; do not full AST as co-equal ship.

## Findings

### F1 — Sanitize inside exported detectors (or one shared wrapper they all call)
class: sharpens-framing
evidence: Prefer-A says strip once at the commit-shape entry before `commandHasGitCommitSubcommand` / index-mutating / checkout-retarget / prospective cover. Production entry is `decideProspectiveGitCommitScopeCover`; unit tests call the exported detectors on raw strings (`dispatcher.test.ts` #5656 cases). Prefer-A proof fixtures name those same detectors for the heredoc non-match.
failure mode: Strip only inside `decideProspective…... while exported helpers stay raw → fixtures that call helpers diverge from production, or green helper tests leave the live false-positive.
disposition: Bound can bind; sharpen the limb to require one shared sanitize used by every exported detector (and thus by the entry), so entry and fixtures cannot diverge.

### F2 — Share the authz preprocess chain, not only the heredoc symbol
class: sharpens-framing
evidence: Authz call sites run `zipShellWithoutHereDocBodies(zipShellWithoutLineContinuations(command))`. Prefer-A Bound names only `zipShellWithoutHereDocBodies`. Authz fixtures already cover continued-delimiter forms.
failure mode: Line-continued heredoc openers stay unrecognized; body text that names a commit still false-refuses after Prefer-A lands.
disposition: Bound can bind; sharpen the share limb to the same preprocess chain (line-continuations then heredoc), matching authz.

### F3 — Scope Issue Expected “other string literals” as residual
class: sharpens-framing
evidence: Issue Expected says quoted heredoc bodies and other string literals must not trip the commit check. Prefer-A Bound is heredoc-only; Reject already parks obscured non-heredoc forms as residual.
failure mode: Silent under-delivery vs Expected, or later scope creep into quote-aware compound splitting under this ticket.
disposition: Bound can bind; state operatively (Reject or leftover footnote) that non-heredoc string-literal mentions stay residual for this conflict_group.

## Injection / swarm lens

Classifier input is untrusted Bash command text (authority-adjacent gate). Over-strip → false allow of a real commit. Deterministic control is Prefer-A as written once F1/F2 land: reuse the authz recognized-heredoc lexer, strip before detector split, keep unclosed/obscured residual, and prove real compound commit-with-file plus index-mutating forms still refuse. Reviewer attention is not the control.

## Road-not-taken / steelman

Full shell AST (Reject): stronger “commands the shell will run” semantics across quotes and nesting. Flip only if Prefer-A fixtures still leave material false positives on common agent note forms after the shared strip lands. Quoted-only strip (Reject): would clear the issue’s quoted NOTE repro with less lexer surface, but leaves unquoted heredoc bodies matched — Prefer-A correctly rejects that.

## Verdict

No `blocks-the-design`. Prefer-A mechanism (share authz heredoc strip; apply before #5656 detectors; fixtures for repro + real compound + index-mutating forms; keep #6185 out) relieves P1–P3. Absorb F1–F3 as Bound sharpening (or Reject/leftover for F3) under KISS/#5783 — short limb wording, not a second design essay.

## Summary

The #5656 commit-shape check in the PreToolUse Bash hook matches the commit command anywhere in the raw command text, including inside a quoted heredoc body. A Bash call that only appends notes to a file outside the repository, and runs no git command, is refused when the note mentions a commit command.

Directive version: 0.129.6. Host: Claude Code.

Note: this report writes the command as `<git-commit>` because the bug itself refuses any Bash call, including the one that files this issue, whose text contains the literal command.

## Repro

```sh
cat >> /path/outside/repo/notes.md <<'NOTE'
- the hook refuses `cd <wt> && <git-commit> -F <file>`; a standalone commit works
NOTE
```

(with the real command text in place of `<git-commit>`)

Result:

```
Directive denied Bash: <git-commit> -a/--all/-am/--include or pathspecs change the file set after the pre-tool index snapshot (#5656). Stage the intended paths first (git add …) then commit with -m/-F only — no -a/--all and no trailing pathspecs.
```

No git command runs. The heredoc delimiter is quoted, so the shell neither expands nor executes the body.

## Expected

The check classifies only commands the shell will run. Text inside a quoted heredoc body, or inside other string literals, is not refused by the commit check.

## Impact

Agents recording what they learned (memory files, notes, issue bodies) are refused when the note names the command that failed. They then reword the text or switch tools, which hides the real cause from the next reader.

## Related

#6185 (follow-up comment): the same check also refuses a commit inside a compound command (`cd <wt> && <git-commit> -F <file>`), so agents whose shell cwd does not persist between calls cannot commit. That looks like the same matcher.
